title: Gorenstein characterization conjecture for normal homogeneous subrings of graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with homogeneous subring $S$, and assume that $S$ is normal. Say that $G$ is **unmixed** when all its relevant minimal vertex covers have the same cardinality, and let a **strong $\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil$-$\tau$-reduction** mean a strong reduction of the indicated size. **Gorenstein characterization conjecture.** Under the assumption that $S$ is normal,

$$
S\text{ is Gorenstein}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G\text{ is unmixed with a strong }\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil\text{-}\tau\text{-reduction}.
$$

This connects the commutative-algebraic property of being Gorenstein with a combinatorial reduction of the graph. The supplied parser gives no resolution evidence, so the conjectural characterization remains open here.
source_name: Lourdes Cruz, Enrique Reyes and Jonathan Toledo, “Gorenstein homogeneous subrings of graphs”, arXiv:2110.05253 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05253

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).
